description: List the top 10 films by share of inventory copies, returning exactly 10 rows and choosing arbitrarily among films tied at the cut.

c.request: What are the top 10 films by number of copies in our inventory? For each, show the `film_id`, how many copies we have, and what share of all inventory copies that is (copies divided by the total number of copies, unrounded), with the highest share first. List the top 10 films by share of inventory copies, returning exactly 10 rows and choosing arbitrarily among films tied at the cut.
c.sql: SELECT i.film_id, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies, COUNT(i.inventory_id) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory) AS share FROM inventory i GROUP BY i.film_id ORDER BY share DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: Return exactly 10 films ranked by copy share (film copies ÷ total inventory copies), ordered by share descending, breaking ties at position 10 arbitrarily, showing film_id, copy count, and unrounded share.
b.sql: SELECT i.film_id, COUNT(*) as copy_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory) as share FROM inventory i GROUP BY i.film_id ORDER BY share DESC LIMIT 10
b.raw: Return exactly 10 films ranked by copy share (film copies ÷ total inventory copies), ordered by share descending, breaking ties at position 10 arbitrarily, showing film_id, copy count, and unrounded share.

d.request: Rank films by their share of total inventory copies in descending order, return exactly 10 rows with arbitrary tie-breaking at position 10, showing film_id, inventory count, and unrounded share proportion.
d.sql: SELECT film_id, COUNT(*) as inventory_count, COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory) as share_proportion FROM inventory GROUP BY film_id ORDER BY share_proportion DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: For each film in the inventory, show its `film_id`, its number of copies (inventory records), and its share of all inventory copies (its copy count divided by the total number of copies across all films, unrounded). Sort from highest share to lowest and return exactly the top 10 films; if several films tie at the cutoff, any of them can fill the remaining spots.
a.sql: SELECT film_id, COUNT(*) AS copy_count, COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory) AS share FROM inventory GROUP BY film_id ORDER BY share DESC LIMIT 10
